V. IMPACT OF PROJECT AND PROJECT ACTIONS
1. General
The probable impact of the project involves consideration of physical, social/economic and aesthetic environments. In order to analyze the interrelationships of impacting actions and altered elements a matrix was constructed. This matrix presents a summary of the project's interrelationships, with the environment, over a space/time continuum.
Interrelationships of note are discussed in the ensuing text. A special category has been added at the end of the matrix. It deals with the relationship that the 100 year flood plain has to the project.
The reader should enter the matrix from the left. For instance, to determine the impacts of the project on animal life, one would read from left to right to learn that residential and business relocation, demolition, grading, construction, etc. nave impacts. The relative impact of the interaction is described symbolically as follows:
a. An o indicates a minor negative impact
b. An O indicates a major negative impact
c. An indicates a minor positive impact
d. An indicates a major positive impact
e. An indicates an undetermined impact
Where an environmental impact is not significant to be termed minor or major, such as urban soils, no specific symbol has been designated. The discussion of probable environmental impacts follows the summary shown in the matrix from left to right beginning with noise levels.
